correctness.rationale: The odds-ray representation \(F_i=P_0o_i\) reduces equality of nonzero fingerprints to equality of a scalar function \(h(u)=u/\prod_j(1+ur_j)\). Its derivative has sign \(1-\sum_jp_j(u)\), proving injectivity on the stated domain. The homogeneous fold gives the converse cube threshold. At the boundary, singleton discrepancy is quadratic in \(\varepsilon\) while total variation is at least the linear marginal difference \(\varepsilon\). Edge case \(F=0\) is handled because all parameters are strictly below one.

value.rationale: The singleton slice is a concrete low-complexity proxy used in the recent Bernoulli-TV program. Establishing its exact identifiability threshold and separating injectivity from Lipschitz stability gives a sharp obstruction: any method relying only on labeled one-success masses must fail uniformly at \(1/n\) and fails even to identify parameters above it. This is a motivated structural boundary rather than an arbitrary parameter exercise.
